## Summary

Update the development base image on `main` to `nvcr.io/nvidian/nemo:fw-base-26.12.rc0`. Keep the GitHub pin, Dockerfile default, and GitLab amd64/arm64 dev rows aligned; LTS pins are unchanged.

Authenticate GitHub builds to NGC using `NGC_API_USER` and `NGC_API_KEY`, following [Export-Deploy's workflow](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Export-Deploy/blob/b0688b2a064a75604b0df8b7553ae052fefe05f4/.github/workflows/cicd-main.yml). Pass only those secrets through both shared-build callers.

The image introduces PyTorch 2.15 and Triton 3.9. Compatibility changes address observed CI failures while retaining those versions and the image's CUDA stack:

- Remove FLA 0.5.1's stale `BT` autotune key; validate the CP kernel import during the build.
- Install a guarded block-pointer lowering adapted from [SGLang #45470](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45470), with Apache-2.0 attribution in the vendored file. It reconstructs block-pointer loads/stores using ordinary pointer operations on Triton versions that removed the API; native implementations are left untouched. This supports the pinned FLA and existing GDP kernels without a Triton downgrade.
- Backport [FlashAttention #2787](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2787) in the dev image for its bundled CuTe code to use `cute.arch.sub_packed_f32x2` with the existing Quack 0.6.5 pin. Add a dedicated GB200 GDP numerical unit bucket.
- Set `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` in the dev image to retain the previous lazy process-group behavior. The previous CI run hit eager-communicator memory exhaustion and NCCL split errors matching [PyTorch's upstream investigation](https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/9006).
- Scope the existing TE pickle opt-in to the two routing-replay tests that load the same CI-managed DeepSeek checkpoint as their already opted-in sibling tests.
- Propagate non-strict model-load exceptions while preserving the existing strict-to-non-strict TE compatibility fallback. A strict control exposed a swallowed legacy-extra-state rejection in the inference-optimized SwiGLU fixture; enable the same fixture-scoped opt-in used by its trusted siblings. Its existing numerical reference is unchanged. Two regression cases cover error propagation.
- Restore the conditional CTA barriers around release/acquire signaling from [upstream Kraken](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/kraken/blob/819d403b439c7fcb2ca15319dfb3ca9b63f5baee/kraken/_ptx_utils/symm_mem_barrier.py). The omitted barriers let only the participating lanes order memory while the rest of the CTA could advance. Focused validation completes all 99 warmups on GB200 and GB300 and passes all 12 existing NVFP4 MoE tests. Add two 64-token NVLS graph replay/refresh variants. The preceding a08 GB200 inference bucket passes all 14 NVFP4 MoE cases, including both new NVLS variants. These cases require Blackwell; H100 coverage is inapplicable.
- Correct MFSDP profiler attribution to group all runtime correlations under their enclosing collective operation and ignore uncorrelated asynchronous annotations. Preserve correlated zero-kernel groups and collective-count assertions.
- Isolate the FSDP buffer-peak test from version-dependent GEMM scratch while retaining its original three/four-full-buffer bounds. Correct ZeRO-1 accounting for the full persistent Partial gradient and its sharded optimizer view, take the baseline after clearing process-global cuBLAS caches, and derive the first-step peak from backward and Adam buffer lifetimes. The 1 MiB accounting slack is unchanged.
- Give the four marked GB200 CP/pipeline CUDA-graph replay cases their own process to bound accumulated communicator state. The catch-all excludes that file automatically; all tests, numerical assertions and existing timeouts remain enabled.
- Run the 19-minute KDA matrix in its own H100 bucket to keep the progressing broad SSM suite within its existing job budget. Preserve current/legacy coverage and timeouts.
- Add compiler coverage (including ordinary-pointer passthrough) and exact GPU replay checks for strided/negative offsets, advance loops, 2-D/3-D boundary masks, transposed layouts, and FP8 padding, plus CPU profiler regression tests.

## Validation

Current head: `cb66709dabef6279d60d7fca2e88cef7703e8f04`. The latest follow-up moves the four marked GB200 CP/pipeline CUDA-graph replay cases into a fresh process after rank 2 hit an NCCL 2.32.5 CUDA out-of-memory error during CP isend in the catch-all bucket. Its teardown barrier then timed out; the built-in restart was interrupted by the existing one-hour job limit. The preceding `a08eed25a5` revision completed **57 successful unit jobs and 1 cancelled GB200 job**. The isolation preserves all 44 marked GB200 test files exactly once and keeps every assertion and timeout unchanged; full coverage now comprises **59 unit buckets**. Fresh GitHub L1/n5 and internal MR/nightly validation are pending on this exact revision. The preceding `a08eed25a5` validation reports GDP numerical tests on H100 and GB200 (63 each); GB200 inference (46 passed / 2 skipped / 2 xfailed, all 14 NVFP4 MoE variants); H100 MFSDP v2 (365 passed / 53 skipped / 7 deselected); H100 kernel determinism (764 passed / 45 skipped / 2 xfailed / 7 xpassed, all 20 Triton compatibility cases). The general H100 bucket passes 4,670 tests (151 skipped / 134 deselected, 19 subtests passed), including both new strict=False/True checkpoint-error propagation regressions; its experimental selection reports 24 passed. KDA passes all 60 tests in 19m21s. Those results do not establish a pass for this new revision.

- Four CPU profiler regression tests pass in the requested-base smoke image, including an uncorrelated asynchronous annotation regression.
- Real Triton 3.9 compilation passes for 32 variants: four kernels × four dtypes × H100/Blackwell targets. All 20 shim compiler/replay pytest cases passed on each platform in the earlier-head full GitHub run: H100 kernel determinism 764 passed / 45 skipped / 2 xfailed / 7 xpassed; GB200 general 478 passed / 78 skipped / 764 deselected. Existing expected-failure results are retained; no final-head pass is inferred.
- The restored barrier compiles in 16 combinations across Triton 3.8/3.9, SM90/SM100, and four ordering-flag pairs. The production barrier AST matches the focused GPU-tested implementation.
- A smoke image built from the requested base installs the shim successfully and verifies the legacy NCCL creator is selected.
- Ruff, Black, `uv run isort`, `git diff --check`, and Dockerfile build checks pass for the current edits.

- Install a guarded block-pointer lowering adapted from [SGLang #45470](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45470), with Apache-2.0 attribution in the vendored file. It reconstructs block-pointer loads/stores using ordinary pointer operations on Triton versions that removed the API; native implementations are left untouched. This supports the pinned FLA and existing GDP kernels without a Triton downgrade.

A strict control exposed a swallowed legacy-extra-state rejection in the inference-optimized SwiGLU fixture; enable the same fixture-scoped opt-in used by its trusted siblings. Its existing numerical reference is unchanged. Two regression cases cover error propagation.
- Restore the conditional CTA barriers around release/acquire signaling from [upstream Kraken](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/kraken/blob/819d403b439c7fcb2ca15319dfb3ca9b63f5baee/kraken/_ptx_utils/symm_mem_barrier.py). The omitted barriers let only the participating lanes order memory while the rest of the CTA could advance. Correct ZeRO-1 accounting for the full persistent Partial gradient and its sharded optimizer view, take the baseline after clearing process-global cuBLAS caches, and derive the first-step peak from backward and Adam buffer lifetimes. The 1 MiB accounting slack is unchanged.

## Remaining investigation

- Blackwell GDP numerical units exposed 55 passes and 8 failures in the bundled FlashAttention CuTe code calling removed `quack.activation.sub_packed_f32x2`; H100 passed 63. No experimental runtime flags are included.
- The missing Qwen3 fixture reproduces on the exact main base and latest main. This external failure is not counted as a pass.

Two additional H100 inference references remain held. GPT-OSS varies on the original image after strict successful loading: two diagnostic captures have matching sampled parameter/buffer and RNG fingerprints on all eight ranks, matching checkpoint-file samples, and prompt-logprob drift at most 1.34e-5, yet different generated sequences. Sampled fingerprints are not full-tensor hashes. Its token reference is unchanged. SwiGLU strict controls expose a legacy TE extra-state rejection; the scoped trusted-fixture opt-in and error-propagation fix above address that failure. Failed controls and repeatability alone do not establish correctness: both references remain unchanged pending causal resolution. Failed-load captures are excluded from baseline evidence.

+# Adapted from SGLang (Apache-2.0):
+# https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/0b158f75e79696ca87158bf65c20a40393e817e9/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/triton_block_ptr_compat.py
+
+"""Restore ``tl.make_block_ptr`` / ``tl.advance`` on Triton builds that removed them.
+
+The FLA kernels use block pointers, which triton-lang/triton#10833 (Triton 3.9)
+removed. On such builds this rebuilds them
+on plain pointer loads and stores, the same way Triton 3.8 lowered them. Older
+Triton is left untouched.
+"""
+
+import triton.language as tl
+from triton.language import core
+
+try:
+    from triton.language import advance  # noqa: F401
+
+    _HAS_BLOCK_PTR = True
+except ImportError:  # removed in triton-lang/triton#10833
+    _HAS_BLOCK_PTR = False
+
+if not _HAS_BLOCK_PTR:
+
+    @core._aggregate
+    class _BlockPtr:
+        base: core.tensor
+        shape: core.tuple
+        strides: core.tuple
+        offsets: core.tuple
+        block_shape: core.tuple
+
+    _BlockPtr.dtype = property(lambda self: self.base.dtype)
+
+    def _int64(values, sem):
+        return core.tuple([sem.cast(sem.to_tensor(v), tl.int64) for v in values])
+
+    def _materialize(p, boundary_check, sem):
+        tile = [b.value for b in p.block_shape]
+        checked = [core._unwrap_if_constexpr(d) for d in boundary_check]
+        ptrs, mask = p.base, None
+        for dim, extent in enumerate(tile):
+            coord = sem.add(p.offsets[dim], sem.arange(0, extent), True)
+            for _ in range(dim):
+                coord = sem.expand_dims(coord, 0)
+            for axis in range(dim + 1, len(tile)):
+                coord = sem.expand_dims(coord, axis)
+            coord = sem.broadcast_impl_shape(coord, tile)
+            ptrs = sem.add(ptrs, sem.mul(coord, p.strides[dim], True), True)
+            if dim in checked:
+                lo, hi = sem.greater_equal(coord, 0), sem.less_than(coord, p.shape[dim])
+                valid = sem.and_(lo, hi)
+                mask = valid if mask is None else sem.and_(mask, valid)
+        return ptrs, mask
+
+    @core.builtin
